newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean brewery plans $238 mln capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Chilean brewery plans $238 mln capital increase.

text.p: Chilean beer-maker Compania de Cervecerias Unidas said it is planning a $238 capital increase through the issue of new shares, some of which will be sold abroad as American Depositary Receipts.
The company will hold a shareholders meeting on October 24 to approve the increase, said the statement sent to the Securities Superintendency.
CCU did not give details of how it will invest the funds.

Newspaper El Diario said the company may use the funds to take control of local soft drinks producer Ecusa by buying troubled Argentine bottler Buenos Aires Embotelladora's (BAESA) stake in the company.
In 1994, CCU signed a joint venture with BAESA, Argentina's largest Pepsi bottler, which resulted in the setting up of Ecusa to distribute Pepsi in Chile.
Other plans could include investments in Peru, said the newspaper.
